claims.text: At high temperatures, the balance between plastic strain capacity and toughness in fusion plasma-facing alloys is governed by grain-boundary-mediated dislocation dynamics.
Larger grain-boundary spacing in coarse-grained material permits dislocations to travel longer distances.
Extended dislocation motion in coarse-grained material promotes dynamic recovery.
Extended dislocation motion promotes crack-tip blunting and energy dissipation.
Plasticity and dislocation activity ahead of a crack can increase intrinsic crack-initiation toughness.
Grain refinement and the associated high density of grain boundaries restrict dislocation movement.
Fine-grained material undergoes earlier strain localization because grain boundaries restrict dislocation motion.
Restricting dislocation motion reduces crack-tip blunting or shielding and therefore lowers fracture toughness.
Grain boundaries act as both sources and sinks for dislocations.
Grain boundaries regulate the extent of plastic deformation at a crack tip.
Coarse-grained samples should have lower yield strength than fine-grained samples at high temperature.
Coarse-grained samples should have greater plastic strain capacity than fine-grained samples at high temperature.
Coarse-grained samples should have greater fracture toughness than fine-grained samples at high temperature.
Fine-grained samples should exhibit higher yield strength and reduced ductility.
Composition-preserving heat treatments can produce fine- and coarse-grained states without changing phase composition or introducing secondary phases.
The proposed mechanism applies over approximately 600–1200 degrees Celsius and at moderate to high strain rates relevant to fusion plasma-facing components.
Dynamic recrystallization or precipitation may alter the proposed grain-size-dependent balance if activated.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is framed relative to an unperturbed as-cast or initially processed baseline, but the decisive experiment and falsification rule compare coarse-grained directly with fine-grained samples and do not require testing the stated baseline.
